acme-support-jordan: Hey team — our Feb 12 invoice shows ~27k tokens but our private dashboard for the same time window shows ~18k. We noticed the meter agent on prod-meter-07 went briefly offline around 2026-02-12 02:10-02:23 UTC. Can you investigate? I've attached the invoice link: https://acme.example/invoices/2026-02-12

maya: Sorry for the trouble, Jordan. Can you confirm agent version and hostname and the exact window you saw the discrepancy?

acme-support-jordan: Agent v1.14.3, host prod-meter-07, outage approx 2026-02-12 02:10:00 -> 02:23:00 UTC. I can pull logs if needed.

maya: Please paste the head/tail of /var/log/meter-agent.log and run a local ledger dump: `sudo meterctl ledger dump --json --range 2026-02-12T01:50:00Z/2026-02-12T03:00:00Z > /tmp/ledger.json`. Also `sudo meterctl status` output.

acme-support-jordan: Pasting snippets below (redacted):
```
2026-02-12T02:09:58Z INFO seq 12985 appended
2026-02-12T02:10:12Z WARN connection lost to collector, buffering to disk
2026-02-12T02:10:55Z INFO seq 12990 appended
2026-02-12T02:23:12Z INFO agent restart (OOM-restart)
2026-02-12T02:23:13Z INFO seq 13005 appended
```
Ledger head/tail: head_seq=12985, last_local_seq=12990, post_restart_seq=13005
`meterctl status`:
```
Agent v: 1.14.3
Host: prod-meter-07
Buffered events on disk: yes (approx 3.2MB)
Last upload: 2026-02-12T02:09:59Z
Uptime: 1h 12m
```

liam: That looks like a contiguous sequence gap (12991-13004). If buffered batches were compacted or the local index corrupted on restart, the handoff to the ledger can drop a range during replay. We also saw cases where the pricer dedups collapsed many small buffered entries into a single aggregated record and billing counted the aggregated tokens differently. Need disk bundle and WAL to be sure.

alex: Also check NTP/time skew: `timedatectl show -p NTPSynchronized --value` and `chronyc sources`. Large clock jumps during the buffering window can cause misordered writes.

meter-agent-bot: Restart: meter-agent v1.14.3 restarted on prod-meter-07 at 2026-02-12T02:23:12Z (auto-restart). WAL replay started (3 files).

maya: Jordan — looks like the agent restarted mid-buffer and after restart the ledger shows seq resumed at 13005, so events 12991-13004 didn't surface in the central meter; they likely remained in a corrupt/partial segment on-disk. Can you tar the agent data dir for us to analyze: `sudo tar czf /tmp/meter-prod-meter-07.tar.gz /var/lib/meter-agent/*` and upload to our support bucket (s3://redwood-support-uploads/acme/prod-meter-07/). We need WAL + index to attempt offline reconstruction.

acme-support-jordan: Uploading now to s3://redwood-support-uploads/acme/prod-meter-07/meter-prod-meter-07-20260212.tar.gz (perm: private).

liam: Thanks. Once we have the bundle we'll run an offline replay tool to rebuild the missing seq range and compare token totals. If we can reconstruct those events they will be merged into the central ledger and we will reconcile the invoice. If reconstruction fails, we have to estimate by replaying client-side metrics and give a credit if warranted. We've reproduced the truncation locally with `meter-sim --burst 5000 --crash-at 02:10` on a staging node — fix is queued for v1.14.4 to make WAL checkpointing atomic across compaction.

maya: @billing-bot please hold invoice 2026-02-12-ACME until we confirm reconciliation (24-48h estimate). We'll update Jordan when we have the replay results.

billing-bot: Invoice 2026-02-12-ACME status: ON_HOLD by support request.

acme-support-jordan: Thanks, team. Appreciate the hold. Please keep me posted with next steps and whether you need any more logs from prod-meter-07.

maya: Will do. Next actions: (1) eng run offline-replay on uploaded bundle; (2) if replay recovers seqs, merge and rerun pricing pipeline; (3) if irrecoverable, compute estimated tokens from proxy logs and reconcile with credit. I'll follow up in this thread. :handshake:
